mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 3.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction of more than 10% month-over-month predicts a negative S&P 500 return over the next 60 trading days due to weakening consumer demand and construction sector underperformance.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST m/m change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at 90% confidence, or the trigger fires but returns are positive more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO m/m change < -0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes at 95% confidence, or the trigger fires but returns are positive more than 25% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both the federal funds rate and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages by more than 0.75 percentage points within the same month signals a dual shock of higher rates and inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > FEDFUNDS_12MMA + 0.75 AND CPIAUCSL > CPIAUCSL_12MMA + 0.75 in the same month
regime_hint: high inflation and rate hike regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered months at 90% confidence, or the trigger fires but returns are positive more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average by more than 5% for three consecutive months indicates elevated precautionary savings and reduced consumption, which depresses demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > RSAFS_12MMA + 5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at 95% confidence, or the trigger fires but returns are positive more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both the unemployment rate and a fall in payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 0.4% month-over-month signals a significant labor market deterioration, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases AND PAYEMS m/m change < -0.4%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered months at 90% confidence, or the trigger fires but returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between housing starts (HOUST) and S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days exists in a stable growth regime, such that an increase in HOUST above its 3-month moving average predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between HOUST above 3MMA and positive 5-day S&P 500 returns falls below 0.3, or the conditional probability of a positive return given the trigger is not significantly above 50% at 90% confidence.
